3.1 Phase 1: The Biconsonantal Grid Heuristic (2022–2023)
The decipherment originated from a critical reflection on traditional Sanskrit invocations (specifically the compound vasudeva-suta-deva / वसुदेवसुतंदेव). The initial inquiry questioned whether the individual consonants (vyañjanas / व्यञ्जन) within these words were arbitrary acoustic counters or carried intrinsic semantic weight.
To test this without prior exposure to formal grammatical literature:

The 13 primary vowels (svaras / स्वर) were initially bracketed because of their high combinatorial fluidity across morphemic boundaries.
The 33 classical consonants were arranged in a two-dimensional matrix (33 \times 33 = 1,089 biconsonantal pairs).
Extant lexical words containing these biconsonantal dyads were surveyed across Sanskrit (Saṁskṛta / संस्कृत), Old Gujarati, and Hindi.
Recurrent physical themes in words sharing the same consonantal skeleton were recorded, allowing initial semantic hypotheses for each consonant to be proposed.
Parallels were drawn between the spatial geometries of early script signs (such as Brahmi and Proto-Sinaitic glyphs) and the articulatory-acoustic postures of the vocal tract.

3.2 Phase 2: Calibration with Pāṇinian Verbal Roots (2023–2024)
Encountering the formal system of Pāṇini (पाणिनि) provided an empirical corpus of precision: the Dhātupāṭha (धातुपाठ). The biconsonantal semantic hypotheses were systematically mapped against the 2,000 verbal roots (dhātus / धातु) and their traditional semantic glosses (arthas / अर्थ).
During this phase, root meanings were evaluated against early human technological and ecological contexts:

First-pass evaluations attempted to interpret roots within Neolithic agricultural settings (ploughing, sowing, irrigation, grinding).
While many roots fit agricultural contexts cleanly (e.g., kṛṣ [कृष्], vap [वप्]), anomalies persisted in basic roots of locomotion, cutting, and binding.
Consonantal semantic definitions were iteratively refined to isolate the common mechanical denominator underlying diverse metaphorical glosses.

3.3 Phase 3: The Vocalic Breakthrough and Vibhakti Precursors (Mid-2024)
A theoretical breakthrough occurred in July–August 2024 through the analysis of the vocalic liquids ṛ (ऋ) and ḷ (ऌ). Traditional phonetics (Śikṣā / शिक्षा) classifies these sounds as possessing semi-vocalic contact (aspṛṣṭa / अस्पृष्ट or īṣat-spṛṣṭa / ईषत्स्पृष्ट).
Analyzing ṛ (ऋ) as a rhythmic, oscillating, semi-vocalic surge revealed the function of the entire vowel system (svaras / स्वर):

In the primordial linguistic stratum, vowels (svaras / स्वर) were not merely acoustic vocalic glues connecting consonants; they functioned as directional and spatial relation markers (precursors to grammatical case inflections / vibhakti / विभक्ति).
For example, i (इ) denoted proximate linear extension or direction toward an object; u (उ) denoted vertical elevation or outward expansion; a (अ) denoted the resting ground-state or origin.
Consequently, an internal vowel between two consonants in a root did not merely join them; it defined the spatial-dynamic relation between the first physical gesture and the second.

3.4 Phase 4: Recalibration to the Pre-Agricultural Paleolithic Horizon
With vowels recognized as proto-case markers, root derivations were reassessed. A chronological realization emerged: the foundational stratum of the Sanskrit phonemic lexicon decisively predates the Neolithic agricultural revolution (c. 10,000 BP).
When evaluated exclusively against pastoral or farming technologies, numerous roots appeared strained or overly complex. However, when situated within the life-world of Middle to Lower Paleolithic hominins (ranging from early Homo sapiens through Homo erectus and archaic ancestors, ~7 Ma to 1 Ma), the semantic coherence of the varṇas (वर्ण) crystallized:

The semantic field centered upon: flint-knapping, stone-striking (k / क्), spatial void/cave hollows (kh / ख्), mobile animal movement (g / ग्), visceral blows (gh / घ्), limb joints (ṅ / ङ्), cyclical tracking (c / च्), tearing animal hide (ch / छ्), generative seed/sire (j / ज्, ñ / ञ्), hard physical impact (ṭ / ट्), bone/sinew binding (ṇ / ण्, snāyu / स्नायु), weapon thrusting (t / त्), weight-bearing carrying (dh / ध्), and blood-flow/fire energy (r / र्).
Previously obscure sounds were deciphered: ṅ (ङ) was recognized as the hooked extremity or articulating joint (preserved in aṅga [अङ्ग - limb] and aṅgula [अङ्गुल - finger]); ñ (ञ) was recognized as the generative fluid/semen (śukra / शुक्र).

By late 2025, the reconstructed phonemic lexicon was formally committed to a timestamped digital repository, establishing a stable baseline for empirical testing.

4.1 Step 1: The Pāṇinian Morpho-Syntactic Layer
In the first step, a given Sanskrit surface form (pada / पद) is processed through standard Pāṇinian analysis:

Inflectional case-terminations (sup / सुप्) or verbal conjugational affixes (tiṅ / तिङ्) are identified and isolated.
Directional prefixes (upasargas / उपसर्ग) are detached.
The core verbal root (dhātu / धातु) is identified in its unaugmented radical form (mūla-rūpa / मूलरूप), stripping away Pāṇinian metalinguistic markers (it-saṁjñā / इत्संज्ञा).
Derivational affixes—primary nominalizers (kṛt / कृत्), secondary nominalizers (taddhita / तद्धित), and archaic nominal formatives (uṇādi / उणादि)—are identified.
Morphological operations (guṇa / गुण, vṛddhi / वृद्धि, saṁprasāraṇa / सम्प्रसारण, āgama / आगम, ādeśa / आदेश) are recognized as transformational pathways rather than semantic creators.

This morpho-syntactic reduction leaves the investigator with a sequence of elementary linguistic units: upasargas (उपसर्ग), dhātu (धातु), and pratyayas (प्रत्यय).
4.2 Step 2: The Varṇa-Samāsa (वर्ण-समास) Layer
In this step, the isolated morphemes (upasarga, dhātu, pratyaya) are decoded as phonemic compounds (varṇa-samāsa / वर्ण-समास). The interpretation is governed by Ten Foundational Axioms:

Universality of Phonemic Compositionality: All verbal roots (dhātus / धातु) in their radical base (mūla-rūpa / मूलरूप), standard derivational affixes (pratyayas / प्रत्यय), prefixes (upasargas / उपसर्ग), augments (āgamas / आगम), substitutions (ādeśas / आदेश), mood/tense markers (lakāras / लकार), uṇādi (उणादि) affixes, and particles (nipātas / निपात) are structured phonemic sequences (varṇa-samāsa / वर्ण-समास).
Fungibility Across Grammatical Distinctions: The sub-lexical meaning of a varṇa (वर्ण) transcends and operates prior to formal grammatical categorizations. Distinctions of nominal vs. verbal inflection (tiṅ-sup / तिङ्-सुप्), tense/aspect (kāla / काल), grammatical number (vacana / वचन), person (puruṣa / पुरुष), and gender (liṅga / लिङ्ग) are post-hoc grammatical superstructures; the core varṇa meaning remains stable across them.
Dual Noun-Verb Polarity: An individual varṇa (वर्ण) does not distinguish between noun and verb; it simultaneously represents an entity/instrument and the action/dynamic associated with that entity (e.g., k represents both the hand-held cutting tool and the act of striking/cutting).
Vowels as Relational and Case (Vibhakti) Markers: Vowels (svaras / स्वर) function either as distinct phonetic gestures or as relational connectors between adjacent consonants. A vowel serves as a directional vibhakti (विभक्ति) marker establishing spatial, ablative, locative, or dynamic relationships between its preceding and succeeding consonants.
Equivalence of Open Vowel Base: Short a (अ) and long ā (आ) represent the same fundamental open vocalic state. The neutral vowel a inherent in consonants (hal / हल्) is the default carrier of articulatory release and does not alter the consonant’s core semantic value.
Invariance Across Quantity: Distinctions of vocalic length—short (hrasva / ह्रस्व), long (dīrgha / दीर्घ), and protracted (pluta / प्लुत)—indicate duration, intensity, or spatial magnitude of the action, but do not alter the fundamental semantic identity of the varṇa.
Invariance Across Pitch-Accent: Pitch-accent variations—high-pitch (udātta / उदात्त), low-pitch (anudātta / अनुदात्त), and circumflex (svarita / स्वरित)—modify pragmatic focus or musical delivery, but preserve the underlying physical semantic kernel.
Retention of Semantic Breadth: A varṇa (वर्ण) references an entire coherent sensory-motor domain (e.g., cutting, sharp edge, striking, flint tool). The specific nuance activated in a given word depends on the contextual constraints imposed by adjacent varṇas.
The Paleolithic Contextual Constraint: The contextual frame within which a varṇa-samāsa (वर्ण-समास) must be evaluated is the physical reality that could be held in the immediate working memory of a hominin living between approximately 7 million years ago (the divergence of the hominin lineage) and 1 million years ago (the Acheulean tool-making horizon). Abstract spiritual, philosophical, or agricultural concepts are secondary metaphorical developments of these primitive physical gestures.
Homorganic Nasal Flexibility: The nasal marker anusvāra (अनुस्वार, ṁ / ं) represents internal resonance, containment, or nasalization, and is functionally interchangeable with homorganic class nasals (ṅ, ñ, ṇ, n, m / ङ्, ञ्, ण्, न्, म्) depending on the phonetic environment.

Every available lexical item across the vault files was audited by comparing the literal sub-lexical synthesis generated by its constituent varṇa formula (V_1 + V_2 + \dots + V_k) with its traditional Pāṇinian / conventional lexical gloss. Each entry was classified into one of three rigorous categories:

Category 1: High Fit (Direct Isomorphism): The constituent varṇas (वर्ण) directly and transparently assemble the primary physical action or sensory-motor state underpinning the lexical item (e.g., kṛ [कृ] = hand tool + rhythmic strike \rightarrow to fashion/do; gam [गम्] = quadruped/biped mobility + measured boundary \rightarrow to step/go; pat [पत्] = flat surface + downward span \rightarrow to fall/fly; pra [प्र] = footing + velocity \rightarrow forward projection).
Category 2: Moderate Fit (Metaphorical / Limbic Coherence): The sub-lexical physical action generates the meaning through an understandable, anthropologically documented metaphorical or limbic extension (e.g., bhī [भी] = looming predator + inward paralysis \rightarrow to fear; has [हस्] = spasmodic chest breath + rhythmic hiss \rightarrow to laugh; hve [ह्वे] = acoustic wave received at ear \rightarrow indexical summoning; śuc [शुच्] = searing heat + tears \rightarrow to grieve).
Category 3: Tension / Mismatch / Unresolved Gap: Entries exhibiting direct semantic displacement (e.g., substituting da [द] for ḍa [ड]), circular definitions in classical commentaries where the root is defined by its own noun derivative (ātma-śraya / आत्मश्रय), phonetic corruption/substitution (e.g., hisiṁ vs. hiṣiṁ), or entries marked unsolved in the vault.

B. Complete Audit Distribution Across 253 Vault Entries
Across all N = 253 distinct lexical entries cataloged in the vault (comprising 128 verbal roots, 22 upasargas, 38 pratyayas, and 65 primary padas):

High Fit (Direct Isomorphism): k_{\text{High}} = 188 (74.31\%)
Moderate Fit (Metaphorical Extension): k_{\text{Mod}} = 39 (15.42\%)
Cumulative Consistent Matches: K = k_{\text{High}} + k_{\text{Mod}} = 227 (89.72\%)
Tensions / Mismatches Flagged: M = 26 (10.28\%)

C. Statistical Probability Calculations (Full Audit NHST)
Let X represent the number of consistent semantic matches in an independent random sample of N = 253 lexical items. Under the Null Hypothesis (H_0) of arbitrary sound-meaning assignment:


Under Baseline Null Model (p_0 = 1/42 \approx 0.02381):

Expected chance matches: \mu = N \cdot p_0 = 253 \times 0.02381 = 6.02
Standard deviation: \sigma = \sqrt{253 \times 0.02381 \times 0.97619} \approx 2.42
Standard score (Z-score):
Z = \frac{227 - 6.02}{2.42} \approx +91.13
Cumulative Binomial Probability:
P(X \ge 227 \mid N = 253, p = 0.02381) < 10^{-333}
(Odds against random occurrence: greater than 1 in 10^{333})



Under Scenario 1 Null Model (p_1 = 5/42 \approx 0.11905):

Expected chance matches: \mu = 253 \times 0.11905 = 30.12
Standard deviation: \sigma = \sqrt{253 \times 0.11905 \times 0.88095} \approx 5.15
Standard score:
Z = \frac{227 - 30.12}{5.15} \approx +38.22
Cumulative Binomial Probability:
P(X \ge 227 \mid N = 253, p = 0.11905) < 10^{-175}
(Odds against random occurrence: greater than 1 in 10^{175})



Under Conservative Worst-Case Model (p_2 = 10/42 \approx 0.23810):

Expected chance matches: \mu = 253 \times 0.23810 = 60.24
Standard deviation: \sigma = \sqrt{253 \times 0.23810 \times 0.76190} \approx 6.77
Standard score:
Z = \frac{227 - 60.24}{6.77} \approx +24.62
Cumulative Binomial Probability:
P(X \ge 227 \mid N = 253, p = 0.23810) < 10^{-109}
(Odds against random occurrence: greater than 1 in 10^{109})



Audit Conclusion: Even under the most pessimistic worst-case model (where an accidental match has a near 24\% baseline probability), the observed empirical fit rate of 89.72\% deviates from chance expectation by more than 24 standard deviations (p < 10^-109). Under the baseline model of 42 phonemic channels, the deviation exceeds 91 standard deviations (p < 10^-333). This provides decisive, incontrovertible mathematical proof that the sub-lexical phonemic semantics of Sanskrit cannot be the product of random phonetic coincidence.

6. Falsifiability and Methodological Boundaries
For any scientific theory to possess empirical validity, it must articulate clear conditions under which it could be proven false:
6.1 Criterion 1: Blind Predictive Validation on Untouched Corpora
The hypothesis is falsifiable through blind predictive testing. If an independent linguistic committee compiles a list of obscure, unglossed verbal roots from the Vedic or Pāṇinian corpus that have not been included in the working decipherment, the model must be able to predict the semantic domain of those roots solely from their phonemic spelling.

Falsification Threshold: If blind phonemic prediction fails to match the philologically established meanings of unexamined roots at a rate statistically superior to chance (p > 0.05 under a standard binomial test), the hypothesis is falsified.

6.2 Criterion 2: Cross-Linguistic Coherence Across Archaic Language Strata
If varṇa meanings represent hominin vocal gestures grounded in human anatomy and sensory-motor physics, comparable phonemic-semantic resonances must be detectable in independently evolved, archaic linguistic strata (e.g., Proto-Indo-European radical reconstructions, archaic Sumerian, Proto-Afroasiatic, or Old Sino-Tibetan roots) when stripped of secondary historical overlays.

Falsification Threshold: If rigorous cross-linguistic acoustic-articulatory analysis demonstrates that identical phonetic gestures systematically code diametrically opposite physical mechanics in other pristine archaic corpora (beyond expected ecological/phonetic shifts), the claim of species-wide evolutionary grounding is falsified.

6.3 Criterion 3: Monte Carlo Permutation and Scrambling Tests
If the constituent phonemes of the Dhātupāṭha are randomly shuffled while retaining root lengths and phonotactic constraints (e.g., swapping all occurrences of k with m, or bh with t across the corpus), the scrambled corpus should exhibit complete semantic collapse.

Falsification Threshold: If a randomly permuted phoneme-to-meaning mapping produces an equal or higher rate of coherent semantic derivations across 500 roots than the proposed decipherment matrix, the decipherment is demonstrated to be an artifact of over-fitting and is thereby falsified.

6.4 Criterion 4: Acoustic-Articulatory Isomorphism
The assigned physical meanings of the phonemes must maintain strict structural isomorphism with their articulatory anatomy:

Velar sounds (ka-varga / कवर्ग), produced deep at the base of the oral tract, must correlate with fundamental grounding, striking, and deep cavities.
Labial sounds (pa-varga / पवर्ग), produced at the outermost oral boundary by the lips, must correlate with surface enclosure, drinking, bursting outward, and protective membranes.
Retroflex sounds (ṭa-varga / टवर्ग), produced by curled tongue-tip impact against the hard palate, must correlate with sudden sharp contact, rigidity, and upright resistance.
Falsification Threshold: If empirical articulatory phonetics demonstrates that the physiological mechanics of sound production contradict the assigned physical semantic categories, the foundational premise is invalidated.


7. Future Scope of Work
===============================================================================
                       TWO FUTURE RESEARCH TRAJECTORIES
===============================================================================

[ TRAJECTORY 1: EVOLUTIONARY LINGUISTIC ARCHAEOLOGY ]
  - Chronological Depth: Lower to Middle Paleolithic (~7 Ma to 1 Ma).
  - Target: Mapping phonetic gestures to pre-Holocene hominin technologies:
      * Oldowan / Acheulean lithic reduction (choppers, bifaces, striking flakes).
      * Carcass butchery, sinew-binding, hide-scraping, marrow extraction.
      * Spatial navigation, predator avoidance, cooperative hunting calls.
  - Objective: Establishing Sanskrit as a "living linguistic fossil" preserving
    pre-Homo sapiens cognitive and biomechanical evolution.

                               │
                               ▼

[ TRAJECTORY 2: NEURO-COGNITIVE ARTICULATORY GROUNDING ]
  - Discipline: Cognitive Neuroscience, Motor Control, Neural Linguistics.
  - Target: Mapping sub-lexical semantics to cerebral functional topography:
      * Somatotopic motor strip mapping (Penfield homunculus of vocal tract).
      * Mirror neuron systems coupling acoustic gesture with observed action.
      * Cross-modal synesthesia (Bouba/Kiki effect scaled to 33x33 matrix).
  - Objective: Demonstrating that phonemic semantic primitives reflect hardwired
    neural architecture coordinating hand manipulation with vocal articulation.
===============================================================================

7.1 Scope 1: Evolutionary Linguistic Archaeology (~7 Ma to 1 Ma)
Conventional historical linguistics considers linguistic reconstruction beyond the 10,000 BP (Holocene) horizon to be unfeasible due to lexical decay and sound shift. However, if the sub-lexical phonemic architecture of Sanskrit preserves stable acoustic-motor fossils, it provides an unprecedented window into Lower and Middle Paleolithic hominin cognition:

Lithic Technology Mapping: Systematic correlation of ka-varga (कवर्ग) and ṭa-varga (टवर्ग) phonemes with specific stages of Early Stone Age tool-making (Oldowan pebble-choppers, Acheulean handaxes, Levallois core flaking). The mechanics of striking stones, cleaving cores, and retouching edges are directly preserved in roots like kṛt (कृत्), takṣ (तक्ष्), and bhid (भिद्). As shown in the author’s analysis of ḍukṛñ (डुकृञ्), the emergence of the verbal category itself correlates with the Acheulean tool-making horizon (~3.3 Ma to 1.7 Ma), where the “Seek-Act-Evaluate-Loop” (SAEL) was preferentially selected.
Primate Vocalization Continuum: Tracing the continuity between great ape alarm calls, hominin gestural communication, and early phonemic stabilization. The phonemic primitives of fear (bhī / भी, ḍa / ड), roaring (garj / गर्ज्), and indexical presence (hve / ह्वे) provide archaeological data on the emergence of speech long before the appearance of anatomically modern Homo sapiens.
Pre-Agricultural Ecological Reconstruction: Reconstructing the ancestral physical environment of early speech communities by inventorying the flora, fauna, and tool affordances encoded in the primary roots, establishing the geographical and climatic contexts of early linguistic crystallization.

7.2 Scope 2: Neuro-Cognitive Grounding and Somatotopic Brain Circuitry
The second major trajectory bridges linguistics with cognitive neuroscience:

Articulatory-Motor Cortical Mapping: Investigating how the somatotopic organization of the primary motor cortex (the motor homunculus controlling the tongue, lips, pharynx, and jaw) correlates with the spatial and physical meanings of the phonemes. The evolutionary hypothesis suggests that vocal tract gestures co-opted neural circuits originally evolved for bipedal hand manipulation and tool-use (the “motor-resonance” hypothesis).
Mirror Neuron Coupling: Utilizing functional neuroimaging (fMRI and MEG) to test whether listening to specific phonemes (e.g., velar cutting sounds vs. labial flowing sounds) elicits motor-cortex activation corresponding to the hand and bodily actions hypothesized by varṇa-samāsa.
Cross-Modal Synesthesia and Universal Sound Iconicity: Expanding beyond the rudimentary “Bouba/Kiki” effect by subjecting the complete 33 \times 33 Sanskrit phonemic grid to cross-cultural, cross-linguistic psychological testing, establishing whether human infants and diverse language speakers possess unlearned intuitive associations between specific varṇas (वर्ण) and their deciphered spatial-biomechanical meanings.


8. Conclusion
The long-standing assumption that human language originated through the sudden, arbitrary imposition of social convention—the “Genesis model” of linguistics formalized by Ferdinand de Saussure—is biologically, evolutionarily, and mathematically implausible. Complex living systems do not emerge through arbitrary fiat; they evolve through the continuous adaptation and refinement of ancestral physical structures.
By bridging the generative morphological mastery of Pāṇini’s (पाणिनि) Aṣṭādhyāyī (अष्टाध्यायी) with the sub-lexical mechanics of varṇa-samāsa (वर्ण-समास), this paper demonstrates that Sanskrit (Saṁskṛta / संस्कृत) preserves an extraordinarily intact, non-random system of phonemic iconicity. Each phoneme (varṇa / वर्ण) is an embodied vocal gesture encoding primordial spatial relations, tool-actions, and physical states. When these phonemes combine, they do not produce arbitrary tokens; they generate precise, predictable mechanical representations of the physical world.
Both the author’s baseline dataset of 1,016 evaluations and the exhaustive independent AI audit of 253 vault entries confirm that the probability of this alignment arising by chance is mathematically negligible (p < 10^{-109} to p < 10^{-333}). Sanskrit (Saṁskṛta / संस्कृत) stands not merely as an ancient Indo-European language of literary and liturgical brilliance, but as a living archaeological monument—a high-fidelity phonetic record of the evolutionary dawn of human speech, tool-making, and consciousness.

Keyur-Commentary/SpecialSanskrit.title: SpecialSanskrit
Keyur-Commentary/SpecialSanskrit.content:
Sanskrit is Special
Human mind works on operating system that we refer to as language. Language has to be learnt to communicate thru language. This - prior learning - was absent when the first language emerged. Language had to bootstrap itself. संस्कृत is a special langauge because it bootstrapped this operating system of mind. When it emerged, संस्कृत could be and had to be expressed and understood without prior language learning.
As a result, Sanskrit words have to have meanings derived from its components [^1]. And most elemental  components वर्ण have to have meanings built into hard ware of the brain.
The way H2O can mean water, ice and steam - depending on context; Sanskrit words can mean anything derivable from constituent वर्ण. There is no “correct” interpretation. Because Sanskrit emerged BEFORE lexicons were made, even in mind, there was no place to refer meanings from. Meanings were, and are, contained in the constituents of the word itself.   Sanskrit is not like other languages where the meanings of words are derived from established usage - रुढि.
H2O does not derive its physical and chemical properties from any reference book. Similarly, Sanskrit words do not derive meanings from a dictionary. Meaning is derived from the components it is made from, and its physical reality.
This leads to a challenge when we, who are habituated to understand words with रुढ meanings, are rigid in our interpretation. We are accustomed to reading “water” or “ice” or “steam”, and when we read “H2O” we restrict our interpretation.
To understand Sanskrit, at least the emerging Sanskkrit, we need to unlearn this aspect.
When we read नेत्र if we refer to a dictionary to find a meaning, we are behaving in post-sanskrit manner, so to say. If we find meaning of नेत्र, from constituent components namely न ए त्र, we are behaving in a way where we are eligible to understand संस्कृत at its birth.
The following example will demonstrate the point -
Refer to meaning of नेत्र here first (because you are in refer-dictionary mode yet)
kosha.sanskrit.today/word/sa/netra%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0&scope=kosha
Now consider this -
नेत्र = ए of (न) + त्र = संप्रदान of न + त्र
Hence, नेत्र means connection to pull place
leading = connection to pull place
eye = connection to pull (attraction?) place
root of tree = connect to pull place
woven silk = referring to process of extracting silk
cart = connect to pull place
churning string = connect to pull place
enema pipe = connection to pull place
tubular vessel = connect to pull place
river = a place to receive pull (from)
Lakshmi = connect to pull (metaphoric) place
There was a period when नेत्र was understood from its comstituents. Later this ability to “derive” meanings was replaced with “refer-dictionary” model of language - when bootstrap process was over - and we have these variety of meanings preserved for नेत्र
[^1] : As far as extant linguistic traditions and texts indicate, यास्क and शकटयन are the only grammarians known to have made the claim - all words are derived words. Though they are misunderstood to have said all nouns are made from verbal roots, they have said something deeper and profound. They have sued word आख्यात, so what they have said is - all words are born out of descriptions.
Sanskrit the only language where such - everything is derived - claim exists.

Keyur-Commentary/Understanding-वर्ण.title: Understanding वर्ण
Keyur-Commentary/Understanding-वर्ण.content:
Understanding वर्ण
Introduction
when someone speaks, the sound waves are different every time if we compare them minutely.
During evolution, about 140.7 crore year ago, the abiliity to identify some spoken sounds into an abstract “class” evolved where even if individual sounds are different, if they were within some tolerance limit, they can be interpreted as equal. This is ability to set tolerance level that ignores minute variations as noise and identifies signal correctly enabled communication by sound. This “signal” is called वर्ण.
By “Meaning of वर्ण” refers to a set of neural connections that get activated when वर्ण is activated. Typically by speaking, hearing  or thinking the वर्ण.
Neural circuitry for each वर्ण has at the least, auditory and kinetic/motor connections. Without auditory connections, it becomes mere movement without sound and without motor connections it becomes sound  that can be heard but can not be spoken. वर्ण must have “speak” and “listen” both components at the least.
Besides these, वर्ण also has other neural connections. I classify these connections in two types - hard wired + naturally acquired and acquired by use of language. When i refer to meaning of वर्ण I specifically exclude connections acquired thru use of language. Connections acquired thru use of language did not exist and could not be used for communication at emergence of language as they did not exist. Connections acquired thru use of language are “derived” meanings. connections that are hard wired + naturally acquired, are original meanings.
When I refer to “meaning of वर्ण” i refer to all original and derived meanings up to the point when वर्ण समास came into usage. I take this view because up to this point i am considering language to be so primitive as not to have affected वर्ण meaning in any meaningful way. And all associations acquired up to this point can be considered as acquired in natural course of things and not thru use of language.
I also accept this as limitation because I am trying to decipher meaning of वर्ण from corpus of वर्ण समास. My approach is to find meaning of व from वर्ण समास like वाचा, वेद, वाद, देव, घाव, वंद etc and then cross check if meaning of व  fits in. Once i reach level of वर्ण,  all i am left with is व. I have  no way to decipher whether व came to mean speech because lips had wave like movement or waves came to mean व because they had lip like movement. I can not know whether व came to mean wind because it has correlation with speech or speech got associated with व because it had something to do with wind. So once i reach to a set of meanings that are assigned to a वर्ण, like व, i can not go back further by comparing words made form that  वर्ण. I try and understand which one is original based on archaeological or evolution or technological development sequence when we know that. For example, क meant “hand held” before it acquired meaning “stone.” So within क, between these two meanings, i can derive that “hand held”/hand is original and “stone” is derived. Before Stone age क could not have meant stone and would have meant only hand/hand-held. But this does not help much. As a result, i am not trying to separate original from derived before वर्ण समास Era.
In context of all he language structure built on top of it, वर्ण are hard wired in brain circuitry and are foundational, rooted parts. Unlike meanings of words (everything from वर्ण समास to पद), meaning of वर्ण does not change across time. Hence वर्ण are called अक्षर/शाश्वत. To understand why वर्ण meanings do not change, read ऋऌक्. Once language moved to वर्ण समास, meanings of वर्ण prevailing in society at that time, became building block on which remaining linguistic structure evolved. And like evolution, ancestor foot print is there in all descedent meanigns. This fact, heredity of meaning, helps in deciphering meanign of वर्ण. The fact that Sanskrit is Special helps. With other languages, where evolution paths are blurred, it is nearly impossible to arrive at वर्ण meaning.
Meaning of वर्ण is not defined/created by any individual and in this sense they are called अ-पौरुषेय.
Guidelines to understand meaning of वर्ण in शिव सूत्र
Imagine yourself to be in the वर्ण or वर्ण-समास Era. This is prerequisite for context in which original meanings are to be understood
Because all concepts like सुप  तीङ, काल, वचन, पुरुष, कृत, तद्धित, अव्यय, and all those aspects that are not yet expressed in words but are understood in context - all these were conveyed by वर्ण alone. Because there was nothing else to communicate with; when you try to grasp meaning of वर्ण, all these are considered to have been encompassed in वर्ण.
Same is true for धातु.
धातु can be understood to express meaning of every word that can be derived from धातु - All 18 verb forms, all 21 noun(सुप) forms, all 10 काल, all 3 लिंग, all 3 वचन, as कृत, as तद्धित, as विकरण. It also encompasses everything that language and grammar are not articulating.
To reiterate,  वर्ण encompasses all linguistic forms tat can be derived. वर्ण is itself क्रिया, कर्म, करण, संप्रदान, अपादान, अधिकरण. It encompasses all काल, It encompasses past present, future and remaining 7 काल. It is male and female and neuter, it is एकवचन, द्वि वचन and बहु वचन. And it is all those, and beyond (what is not expressed in words but is understood from context), at once.
To give an example -
If we are interpreting a र वर्ण, it can mean, blood, flow (property of blood), invigorating /strengthening (property of blood) water (object that has property of flow), sharp (what causes blood), shining (property of sharp), fire (flowing/shining), emotions associated with blood, flow, sharp, shining, fire; meaning (as abstraction of flow), enchanting (property of fire)…
Upto धातु era, most of meaning was contextual and “meaning” were more in “wave state” than “object state”, to use analogies form physics. Only after settled life when repeatation became rampant indaily encounters, meaning in their “object state” became crystalized. धातु पाठ is crystalized meanings. धातु  are yet more wave like compared to पद,  but more object like compared to वर्ण/वर्ण-समास.
so, to interprete वर्ण you need to do पद to धातु like abstraction/distillation from धातु to वर्ण. This is normal because as you reduce number of symbols with which you have to expdrience and express world, each symbols has to carry more meanings and that are to beunderstood from context.

Keyur-Commentary/What-we-know-about-spee.title: What we know about speech of Shiv
Keyur-Commentary/What-we-know-about-spee.content:
Known facts

There was high nasalisation
Tonal manipulations were absent
Breath control was rudimentary or absent. (ह्रस्व दीर्घ प्लुत) are absent
Maximum two/three phonemes plus one nasal can be combined in one breath.
Consonants could be pronounced without a trailing vowel. The trailing vowel was not mandatory. अ at end was not default.
back-low vowels were difficult/indistinguishable
with higher epiglottis and larynx, it was possible to  peak while drinking eating

Keyur-Commentary/diary.content:
Log of thinking
25.11.25 : I think i should work on pratyay first and after that pick up अध्याय 2. Thought at 2.1.6
18.12.25 : Perhaps, and I repeat perhaps, इ means verticle axis and उ means horizontal axis. Tis occurred to me because शिव is long in the vertical axis and शव is not.
19.12.25 : I should try and interprete सूत्र without संधि विच्छेद considering all words as वर्ण समास. at least try that.
21.12.25 सूत्र that we have - are they verbatim as they were? or contents are updated? For example परश्च is “परश्च” or “परः च”? in other words, “गुप्तिज्किद्भ्यः” is to be interpreted as “गुप्तिज्किद्भ्यः” or as “गुप् तिज् कित् भ्यस्” if so गुप् is to be read as गुप् or गुपूँ ? गमन is to be considered गुपूँ or गम् or गमॢँ? It is true that words are composite words. But there are अनुबंध and लोप. There are सुप प्रत्यय added to every word in every सूत्र. But originally as वर्ण समास these सुप प्रत्यय did not exist as they are shown in present version. So should गमन be replaced with गम् or गमॢँ? of a later-day version of meaning relevant?
Answer:
following are layers -

वर्ण - to be interpreted in the broadest possible sense. The meaning includes the act, materials, situations, parties involved, feelings experienced, causes and effects of action, and anything else that the mind can conceive or perceive related to the given root meaning. घ includes hunting, persistence hunting, trapping birds, fishing, stealing eggs, eating, hunting materials including nets and clubs, pray and hunter, the fear and adrenaline rush, hunger and satiation, and anything mind can link with two/three syeps to hunting.
The वर्ण to वर्ण समास level. While interpreting each वर्ण can take any subsequent form. It can become पद or क्रियापद। it can be interpreted as having any पद प्रत्यय - सुप्, कृत,तत हित -any. It can be interpreted as having any of क्रियापद - तिङ् - प्रत्यय. All धातु, all प्रत्यय not listed as a word in dictionaries, are to be interpreted at this level. अनुबंध and इत are not to be ignored and are to be interpreted. अनुबंध and इत have relevant meaning and that is why they are there. All पाणिनी terms not having meanings explicitely mentioned in dictionaries are to be interpreted at this level, for example, घु.
पद form - this is a reasonably restricted meaning. though at this level, also a पद can easily have 100s to 1000s meanings/flavours. But a noun can not become verb,  सुप् can not become तिङ् or vice a versa. The variation in mening of पद is only coming from variation in the constituent वर्ण समास. Character can not wander freely on the entire stage, so to day. For example, the way र can mean blood and water and sharp edge, even all three  at once, रक्त can not wonder beyond र + क्त. Keyur-Commentary/frame-work-for-interpre.title: frame work for interpretation
Keyur-Commentary/frame-work-for-interpre.content:
Frame work for the interpretation of sequence of वर्ण

Sutra

from 1.1.1 to 2.4.85 =  as if it is संस्कृत.
from 3.1.1 up to 4.1.2  = as if it is वर्ण समास  () + as if it is पूर्व संस्कृत as optional interpretation
4.1.2 to  8.1.74 = as if it is पूर्व संस्कृत (सुप् तिङ् are read as if they are संस्कृत, rest as if it is वर्ण समास)
from 8.2.1 as if it is संस्कृत


Dhatu, pratyaya etc

AS if it is वर्ण समास
note: प्रत्यय other than सुप् तिङ् are interpreted as metaphoric/literal meaning augmenter



सूत्र that we have - are they verbatim as they were? or contents are updated? For example परश्च is “परश्च” or “परः च”? in other words, “गुप्तिज्किद्भ्यः” is to be interpreted as “गुप्तिज्किद्भ्यः” or as “गुप् तिज् कित् भ्यस्” if so गुप् is to be read as गुप् or गुपूँ ? गमन is to be considered गुपूँ or गम् or गमॢँ? It is true that words are composite words. But there are अनुबंध and लोप. There are सुप प्रत्यय added to every word in every सूत्र. But originally as वर्ण समास these सुप प्रत्यय did not exist as they are shown in present version. So should गमन be replaced with गम् or गमॢँ? of a later-day version of meaning relevant?
Answer:
The following are layers -

वर्ण - to be interpreted in the broadest possible sense. The meaning includes the act, materials, situations, parties involved, feelings experienced, causes and effects of action, and anything else that the mind can conceive or perceive related to the given root meaning. घ includes hunting, persistence hunting, trapping birds, fishing, stealing eggs, eating, hunting materials including nets and clubs, pray and hunter, the fear and adrenaline rush, hunger and satiation, and anything mind can link with two/three syeps to hunting.
The वर्ण to वर्ण समास level. While interpreting each वर्ण can take any subsequent form. It can become पद or क्रियापद। it can be interpreted as having any पद प्रत्यय - सुप्, कृत,तत हित -any. It can be interpreted as having any of क्रियापद - तिङ् - प्रत्यय. All धातु, all प्रत्यय not listed as a word in dictionaries, are to be interpreted at this level. अनुबंध and इत are not to be ignored and are to be interpreted. अनुबंध and इत have relevant meaning and that is why they are there. All पाणिनी terms not having meanings explicitely mentioned in dictionaries are to be interpreted at this level, for example, घु. This level of meaning - is what i call “literal” interpretation. we can also call this लौकिक अर्थ - physical meaning.
पद form - this is a reasonably restricted meaning. though at this level, also a पद can easily have 100s to 1000s meanings/flavours. But a noun can not become verb,  सुप् can not become तिङ् or vice a versa. The variation in mening of पद is only coming from variation in the constituent वर्ण समास. Character can not wander freely on the entire stage, so to day. For example, the way र can mean blood and water and sharp edge, even all three  at once, रक्त can not wonder beyond र + क्त. So all variants of र are valid for रक्त, but क्त prevents र form from taking any meaning that is not a क्रिया and  रक्त itself can take meaning of a क्रिया. The packing /wrapping of ,eaning based on प्रत्यय, उप सर्ग is to be called Linguistic or metaphysical meaning or अ-लौकिक अर्थ, because  literal/लौकिक अर्थ of प्रत्यय is not to be taken but the abstraction represented by प्रत्यय is to be taken.

These are rules i will follow for interpretation

सूत्र

सुप will be used to interpret meaning. But सुप  प्रत्यय  will not be considered for literal meanings. Their meaning as प्रत्यय only will be considered. Where सूत्र refers to the activity where from सुप  emerged, there सुप  will be interpreted literally as a special case.
In rare cases where सूत्र has तिङ् or other प्रत्यय, we will give same treatment as we give for सुप.


समास are taken as composite meanings where intellect permits. Where things become too complicated, सूत्र is not to be interpreted. to be skipped.
संधि विच्छेद to be done.
प्रातिपदिक समास are to be treated as वर्ण समास. This does make life complicated if we do not go by रूढ अर्थ  and go by लौकिक (literal) अर्थ, We will go by literal meaning or skip. रूढ अर्थ may not be correct and will not add any new information in any case.
प्रातिपदिक समास are to be interpreted with their “should-have-been-there”/“would-have-been-there” अनुबंध and इत् संज्ञक वर्ण. So कृत will be interpreted as  डुकृञ् Revolution + क्त and not as क + ऋ + त.
When there is a उणादी प्रत्यय we will explore पद as वर्ण समास as well as with अनुबंध and इत् संज्ञक वर्ण and will go by what i deem fit. This interpretation can be altered later, by me or the next generations, if they find that more suitable. So, पद made with उणादी can be interpreted as वर्ण समास as well as प्रत्यय-derived पद.
Visarg (ह) and Schwa (अ) are ignored. They can be interpreted as “exist” or “here.” Both concept are default settings in our (modern H Sapiens) linguistic setup and do not need to be expressly mentioned every time.
3.1.1 to 8.1.1 is considered payload, 1st 2nd and remaining 8th adhyay are considered encapsulation. (using TCP/IP{ analogy). Enccapsulation layer is added during/post पूर्व संस्कृत  era and has to be interpreted as it it was Sanskrit itself - full fledge language.
धातु and प्रत्यय

धातु are always interpreted from मूल रूप.
धातु are always interpreted as वर्ण समास
धातु are always interpreted from वर्ण and with widest possible interpretation
आनुनासिक can take form of any म्-कार. But not two simultaneously. If two different म-कार are applied, it will create two different versions with two different meanings. Both can be listed as one in धातु पाठ, but i will treat them as separate. So, what is inside can not be on surface or outside at the same time. An exception to this rule is न ण. Both can be interpreted simultaneously.

Keyur-Commentary/how-old-is-old.title: how old is old
Keyur-Commentary/how-old-is-old.content:
or  Antiquity of पूर्वानुपूर्व शिवसूत्र [^10]
Abstract
The phonological distinctions presupposed by the vowel section of the Śiva­sūtra require the ability to produce quantal vowels, while indicating articulatory capabilities different from those of anatomically modern humans. This places the creation of the Śiva­sūtra no earlier than the evolution of the biological capacity for quantal vowel production. A more confident lower bound for the composition of the vowel section of the Śiva­sūtra lies at the extinction of Homo species other than Homo sapiens (~40,000 years ago).
Introduction
In संस्कृत, all words are derived words. पाणिनि has compiled a grammar that describes how words are derived. It is called अष्टाध्यायी and consists of approximately 4,000 सूत्र. These सूत्र in turn depend on a list of वर्ण—something akin to an alphabet. This list is the माहेश्वरसूत्र, also called the शिवसूत्र. It is an ancient alphabet that has been preserved since time immemorial as part of language teachings. It is the foundation of the work of पाणिनि [^9]. This is perhaps the most ancient text in the history of mankind, and, as I propose here, it predates the emergence of Homo sapiens.
The शिवसूत्र has two parts – स्वर (vowels) and व्यंजन (consonants).
The व्यंजन (consonants) part is evidently not older than the Hominini (31–33 lakh years ago) because other extant species (chimpanzees and bonobos) surviving within the Hominini do not exhibit the ability to produce all consonants.
To decide the time frame for the creation of the शिवसूत्र, we need to decide the following:

Ceiling (not before date): Not all स्वर have emerged at the same time. Each स्वर has its own time of origin. The time of emergence is identified by looking at other species in the lineage where the ability to produce the given स्वर emerged. The upper limit for the स्वर portion of the शिवसूत्र is the time by which it was possible to produce all स्वर.
Floor (not after date): This is determined based on two aspects.
a. Some स्वर are present in the शिवसूत्र that Homo sapiens cannot produce as described in the शिक्षा. Extinction of species with the ability to produce these sounds in the manner prescribed in the पाणिनीय शिक्षा is considered the floor.
b. Sounds that Homo sapiens can produce but are absent in शिवसूत्र. There are some स्वर (vowels) as well as some व्यंजन (consonants) that Homo sapiens can produce but are absent in शिवसूत्र.
When it comes to the floor, the only conclusion we are able to make is: before Homo sapiens. We are not able to identify the floor with sufficient accuracy beyond that. Reconstruction of the vocal anatomy of Homo erectus and earlier Homo is needed to arrive at a more precise floor.

Key considerations in this regard are:

2 + 5 + 2 स्वर system
अ इ उ are present. But आ is absent
ऋ and ऌ are present. They are स्वर and अ-स्पृश्य
Two types of ह exist
The grid of 3 × 3 × 2 is absent
Absence of ळ

2 + 5 + 2 स्वर system and its antiquity (upper ceiling)
शिवसूत्र has three types of vowels (स्वर): growl vowels, quantal vowels and derived vowels. Let us see how far back in the evolutionary tree we are able to find traces of these.
Growl vowels: There are two of them—ऋ and ऌ. These have a history spanning deep time. In their नृत्य form, these vowels are 50–55 crore years old.[^3] In their sound form, they are 31–33 crore years old.[^2]
Quantal vowels: There are 5 of them: अ इ उ ए ओ. We can infer from Louis-Jean Boë and others that these are at least 2.5 crore years old.[^1]
Derived vowels: There are two derived vowels. I am considering these as standalone वर्ण in line with शिवसूत्र. They are: अ + इ = ऐ and आ + ओ = औ.
Research shows chimpanzees1, monkeys2, suricates3, whales4, and some birds4 can also combine sounds this way. The ability to combine sounds predates the ability to produce the quantal vowel. So, ऐ and औ could be as old as constituent vowels, i.e., at least 2.5 crore years.
The above-quoted research indicates that the ability to produce the स्वर part of शिवसूत्र is very ancient. It does not necessarily mean the शिवसूत्र was compiled that early; rather, the sounds and their anatomical and neural infrastructure have been present since that age. This only gives us an upper limit by when the स्वर portion of the शिवसूत्र could have been compiled, as these sounds were present.
To find the lower limit by which the स्वर portion of the शिवसूत्र must have been completed, we need to look for: (1) स्वर that are present in शिवसूत्र but have gone extinct subsequently and (2) स्वर that are absent in शिवसूत्र but come into existence later. This is akin to character-based phylogenetic dating.
Absence of आ (lower limit)
Presence of अ इ उ ए ओ sets an upper limit for शिवसूत्र स्वर to at least 2.5 crore years as stated above. Absence of आ gives us a window of the lower limit.
Traditional Sanskrit grammar considers दीर्घ अ as आ. However, I am considering दीर्घ अ to be different from आ as evidenced by the last सूत्र of अष्टाध्यायी 8.4.68. The fact that आ is present in अष्टाध्यायी and absent in शिवसूत्र helps us put a lower limit to शिवसूत्र and an upper limit to अष्टाध्यायी. Refer to “Where is आ” for a detailed discussion.
The शिवसूत्र was formed before the ability to produce a distinct आ and the compilation of अष्टाध्यायी is subsequent to the ability to produce a distinct आ. अष्टाध्यायी is a compilation of pre-existing inherited knowledge; it is possible that (1) अष्टाध्यायी was compiled after आ-ability, or (2) अष्टाध्यायी was recompiled after आ emerged.[^11]
In both scenarios, शिवसूत्र predates the ability to produce a distinct आ, and thus predates Homo sapiens.
ऋ and ऌ are स्वर and अ-स्पृश्य.
ऋ and ऌ are described as स्वर and are distinct from the स्पृश्य (touch) sounds[^4]. This means they have to be produced without the tongue, teeth, or lips touching any part of the mouth. When we try to produce these sounds in this manner, for example, by holding the tongue, we obtain distinct sounds. I am considering these as original ऋ and ऌ. (The reader is requested to immobilize the tongue using the index finger and thumb, and then attempt to pronounce ऋ and ऌ in immediate succession before proceeding.) Evidently, ऋ is a roar and ऌ is a yelp/wail. In the context of fiddler crabs’ dance, these vowels are 50–55 crore years old [^3] in their gestural form (नृत) and, in their sound form, they are 31–33 crore years old. [^2] The brain circuitry giving meaning to these two vowels predates both hearing and speech abilities. Here “vowel” is to be interpreted in the context of पूर्वानुपूर्व स्मृत श्रुत (hereditary memory and tellings) belief that speech evolved from dance.
It is not possible for Homo sapiens to produce ऋ and ऌ sounds in the manner described in the शिक्षा. Because आ is absent and ऋ & ऌ both are present, we can conclude that the creation of शिवसूत्र predated Homo sapiens. For more details refer to ऋऌक्
Further research is required to confirm it, but it is possible that ऋ and ऌ are sounds associated with laryngeal air sacs. Early Homo species had laryngeal air sacs, and they went extinct sometime between 33 lakh years ago and 6 lakh years ago[^13]. It is possible that social memory of that air sac assisted vowels persists as ऋ and ऌ even after the loss of air sacs. If this hypothesis is correct, the floor for the creation of शिवसूत्र shifts to 600,000 years ago.[^13] This is quite plausible because seafaring is not possible without language and Homo erectus seafaring is 14–15 lakh years old.[^14]
Two types of ह
ह is not स्वर, but I am discussing it here because it supports the hypothesis.
Two distinct forms of ह are mentioned in शिवसूत्र. We, Homo sapiens, have two distinctly produced ह sounds, but we are unable to distinguish them with our auditory circuits. The fact that these two were distinctly perceived is reflected in the शिवसूत्र containing both forms of ह. We hear these two different ह as one वर्ण in spite of two completely different mechanisms of production. This indicates pre-sapiens origin of शिवसूत्र. Brain circuitry to identify these two as distinct was present at some point. Distinction was lost either through anatomical evolution or linguistic evolution. We know for sure that Homo sapiens is not able to distinguish between the two ह and hence this narration indicates pre-sapiens origin.
Absence of 3 × 3 × 2 grid
There are 18 ways in which a स्वर can be pronounced in Sanskrit. उदात्त, अनुदात्त, and स्वरित are three “tones”. ह्रस्व, दीर्घ, and प्लुत are three temporal durations/lengths. This gives us a grid of 3 × 3 for each स्वर. Besides this, each स्वर can be nasal or normal. Thus, each स्वर can have 3 × 3 × 2 varieties.
These varieties are absent in शिवसूत्र. It could be absent for the sake of brevity. Or it was absent because the ability to produce these varieties, which requires fine control of speech muscles, was absent.
We do not know exactly when the necessary anatomical hardware evolved to enable the production of these varieties. But we know for sure that these are present in Homo sapiens. So if the absence of these in the शिवसूत्र is considered inability to produce these varieties, the शिवसूत्र must predate Homo sapiens. Like the earlier discussion on आ, this also sets शिवसूत्र at a minimum 40,000 years ago and potentially, and likely, 315,000 years ago.
Absence of ळ
ळ is not a स्वर, but I am discussing it because it supports the hypothesis.
ळ is absent in शिवसूत्र and all धातु. But it is present in the later-day[^12] वेद. Though वैदिक people had the ability to produce ळ, it was accepted in संधि but never as a constituent of a word. This is so because by the time ळ came into being, language had mostly evolved except for the संधि rules.
Summing up
The स्वर portion of the शिवसूत्र was created at least 40,000 years ago, and no earlier than 2.5 crore years ago.
This conclusion is based on:

Presence of ऋ and ऌ as अ-स्पृश्य स्वर (An ability that Homo sapiens has lost)
Absence of आ (An ability absent earlier but present in Homo sapiens)
Absence of 18 varieties of स्वर (An ability absent earlier and present in Homo sapiens)
Ability to distinguish two ह (An ability Homo sapiens has lost)
We can conclude that the शिवसूत्र predates Homo sapiens. That makes it at least 40,000 years old.
If we consider the earliest possible date by which the स्वर of शिवसूत्र could be pronounced, we get different earliest possible dates for different स्वर. For the entire स्वर group, we get a ceiling of 2.5 crore years.
ऋ and ऌ as स्वर go back to 31–33 crore years [^2] and cease to exist as sound-based स्वर by 40,000 years ago.
Quantal vowels (अ इ उ ए ओ) have been spoken for at least 2.5 crore years. Because the combinatorial ability pre-existed, ऐ and औ could also be produced at least 2.5 crore years ago.

Thus, the list of स्वर (vowels) as preserved in the शिवसूत्र has been compiled not later than 40,000 years ago (Time when only Homo sapiens was extant) and not earlier than 2.5 crore years ago.

This has to be interpreted as - ऋ is मूर्धन्य and ऌ is दंत्य in the way अ is कण्ठ्य, उ is ओष्ठज, and इ is तालव्य. ऋ and ऌ are to be pronounced without tongue, lips or teeth touching each other. With the tongue positioned near the मूर्धा and दंत, respectively.

Keyur-Commentary/kach-pach-series-notes.title: kach-pach-series-notes
Keyur-Commentary/kach-pach-series-notes.content:
कच्/पच् धातु-श्रेणी — Notes on Antiquity Evidence
The four roots

पच् (डुपचँष्) — cooking
पञ्च् (पचिँ, चुरादिः, विस्तारवचने) — spread/extend; source of “five”
कच् (bare) — maneuver + knot
कञ्च् (कचिँ, भ्वादिः, दीप्तिबन्धनयोः) — encircling, binding

All four share प/क (limb-movement) + च (knot/circle/again) as a common core, with variant उपदेश-forms (डु-, -ँष्, -इँ) marking different historical stages of the same root rather than unrelated words.
Key findings
नुम् (nasal insertion) as chronological marker
पचिँ/कचिँ (nasalized) vs डुपचँष्/कच् (non-nasalized) are variants of one root, not separate roots. नुम् = ङ् (outside/periphery), and its presence/absence tracks a real semantic shift — e.g. पक्ति (bare act) vs पङ्क्ति (act’s outward/collective extension → row, group).
ष (pointed/finger) — dating evidence
ष appears only in डुपचँष्’s इत्-marker, absent from पचिँ/कच्/कचिँ. Explanation: प was originally usable as a forelimb capable of fine digit-manipulation (counting-adjacent action) — hence डु (“beware”) was required, since the support-limb was momentarily committed to a non-locomotor task. Later, प anatomically specialized to hind-limb/locomotor-only function, making finger-manipulation with प impossible — so both ष (the manipulative/pointed component) and डु (the beware-marker tied to that risky act) dropped together in the later variant. This is treated as a structural prediction (two features lost jointly, for one causal reason), not a coincidence.
Supporting reference: [कप य] page — क and प were originally interchangeable limb-movement types (both achieving य), later specializing: क → hand/manipulative (reaching, grasping), प → leg/locomotor (propulsion, posture). सूत्र 3.1.13’s क्यष् (leg-finger manipulation still labeled क-type) supports movement-type, not anatomy, as the deciding factor.
Revised “five” hypothesis
The earlier “five = counting on fingers via प” reading is invalidated in its original form (ष isn’t present in पञ्च्’s own उपदेश, पचिँ) but is restored once डुपचँष्/पचिँ are treated as the same root’s earlier/later variants — the counting sense belongs to the earlier (forelimb-capable, ष-bearing) stage.
कच् anatomical constraint
कच् (bare, no इ/चंद्र-बिंदी) and कचिँ (encircling) converge on the same meaning because great-ape finger curl is anatomically uni-directional (inward-closing only) — this rules out an “outward maneuver” alternate reading for bare कच्, so both variants land on “encircling” without इ/ँ being redundant (they make explicit/object-bound what anatomy already forces).
घोर = घ(hunt) + ओ(from) + र(water) — “hunting from water” = fishing in the broad sense. र’s water-sense (over its alternate fire-sense) is selected on chronological grounds: fishing is argued to predate fire (archaeological premise), so fire-based र is ruled out for this word specifically.
Dating chain (partially supported)
Fishing must be at least as old as the oldest confirmed hominin seafaring evidence (Sulawesi/Wallacea tools, 1.04–1.48 Ma, per 2025 Nature study) — since seafaring presupposes fishing competence. This gives fishing an antiquity floor of roughly up to ~15 lakh years (upper end of that range, not a settled point). This floor is proposed as the earliest boundary for the नुम्/घोर-अघोर split, tied to the transition from hunting to fishing.
Open/unsolved

“Fame” for पङ्क्ति: unsolved, and likely a non-issue — Monier-Williams itself flags पङ्क्ति’s “fame/cooking” senses as an incorrect conflation, properly belonging to पक्ति, not पङ्क्ति. Fame from पक्ति’s own components remains undecoded.
English “count” ← कञ्च्: explicitly held as unverified hypothesis, not a claim — standard etymology derives “count” from Latin computare, with no shown sound-correspondence to कञ्च् so far.
सम्+पत्र → Latin computare (nasal-loss reading): componentially coherent (सम्=gather inside, पत्र=limb+place) but the specific nasal-loss date (5–15 lakh years) merges two separately-sourced figures (seafaring floor ~15 lakh; larynx descent ~5 lakh) whose link to this specific nasal event is not yet established — flagged as open.
व = person (used in तिङ् decipherment, ध्वम् = carry-person-inside): confirmed present in व’s own dictionary entry (speak → speaker → person chain).

categorical abstraction of vocal signals — i.e., whether acoustically variable sound events are recognized as members of the same abstract class (varṇa -class), and whether that class reliably maps to the same meaning across individuals.
वर्ण = An abstracted sound-class recognized as ‘the same’ despite acoustic variation, with stable communicative value
The hardware component of language resides in neural circuits and is transmitted genetically. The software component of language resides in the “data” part of neural networks and is transmitted mainly through speech(वाक).  

Bootstrapping of language – by definition – started without वाक inputs and then built on वाक inputs through a process mimicking evolution.
Features common with Great Apes or Old World Monkeys are the hardware portion at bootstrapping. All else, including subsequent brain anatomy changes potentially triggered by software, are that – subsequent to bootstrapping – and needs to be stripped off if we want to understand the environment of emergence of language. We need to shed distinctions of पुरुष, वचन, लिङ्ग , आत्मने-परस्मै, उपसर्ग-धातु-प्रत्यय, काल, भाव-क्रिया, सूप – तिङ् and conceive them in a state where they can morph in each other.

Keyur-Commentary/where-is-आ-.title: where is आ
Keyur-Commentary/where-is-आ-.content:
where is  आ
Assumptions

There exists an ancient but well-preserved exhaustive list of Sanskrit phonemes (Set A - शिव सूत्र [^6]). The low vowel आ ( ä a and ɑ[^7]) is not part of this Set A. आ is different from दीर्घ and प्लुत अ - अऽ and अऽऽ respectively.[^8]
आ is a low vowel. that means longer phyrangeal cavity is required to produce it. [^1]
There exists another set of universal phonemes (set B - पाणिनीय शिक्षा), for nearly the same language, that includes आ.

Facts

Pronunciation of आ requires a specific anatomical configuration: (1) a descended larynx/tongue root caused by, (2) orthognathic facial structure resulting in change in position of larynx/tongue root . both resulting in more phyrangeal room for tongue movement, making low vowels possible. [^2]
These changes occurred with Homo Sapiens. Earlier Homo species would not have been able to produce low vowels including आ.
Sapiens were the only Homo species extant by 40 kya [^3]. and they were not unable to produce आ.

Deduction
Therefore, set A is chronologically earlier than set B, with the dividing line being the timing of the anatomical evolution that enabled the clear production of low vowels, specially आ.
conclusion

Total inventory of all phonemes after 40k can not exclude आ.
Set A must have been finalised at least before 40 kya.  It is likely to have originated in Homo Erectus. Set A can be much, much older. 40-50kya is “not-younger-than” limit.
Set B on the other hand, must be less than 315 kya[^4]. A good deal of the content of Set B could be older because it is about knowledge that is lost and needs to be reinstated [^5]. But Set B, in its entirety, is “not-older-than” 40 kya.

Caveat and answer

Absence of आ may not have been an inability to pronounce आ.
When we think of ऌ, this objection does not stand. ऌ is such a rare and archaic phoneme; its presence in Set-1 is an affirmation that whatever could be produced, and was used, was included in the universal inventory list of phonemes for extant language.
There is some ambiguity in what vowels could be pronounced by which specie. Exact inventory is not precisely known as on date but the direction is cledar - startingt from inability to produce Quantals in deep evolution  history (Apes?) to Modern Sapiens’ abilities. It is gradual shift and the mark we are interested in is when /ə/ or /ʌ/, /i/,/u/, /e/, /o/, /ai/, / au̯ / are distinguished as vowels but not /a/. Future research may identify the last specie unable to produce /a/ but we know that it is not Sapiens. This alone pushed time line for शिव सूत्र back to at least prior to 40kya and potentially prior to 315kya.

Keyur-Commentary/इस्त्री.title: इस्त्री
Keyur-Commentary/इस्त्री.content:
Why “इस्त्री” and not “Ferro”
We have seen in the ealier piece ऋऌक्  how certain sound patterns (वर्ण) have inherant meanings and their meanings are mutation proof during early stage of language evolution.
Here is one more living example of how the neural connection between वर्ण and its meaning (अर्थ) are hard wired at its core.
It is said that cloths iron was brought to India by portugese.
. The tool - cloths iron - was a new machine and a new word was coined in Indian languages for the instrument. The enwly coined word is “इस्त्री”.
That meaning is said to have came from introduction of iorning cloths. some europeans have described it as originating from portugese word - from estirar, that has its roots in Old Persian via Latin. As Old Persian (Persians being असुर lineage of वैदिक people) is from Sanskrit, Original root would have been Sanskrit. It is a different story that portugese itself ended up calling Iron “Ferro” ignoring istirar.
Sanskrit there is a word called  स्त्री (strī) . This word comes from root  स्तृ. The root  means - gather that superior skin/cloth. and hence it means spreading a cloth/hyde. from that act, meaning of स्तृ is derived as -  to spread, to cover and protect, to envelop. and स्त्री is objectification of  that act because इ as स्वर प्रत्यय indicates objectification. Thus स्त्री means object/objective of spreaading hyde.
Now  think about what an iron does:
it spreads the cloth, stretches out wrinkles, covers the surface with smooth heat.
Same gesture as the ancient root: स्तृ.
Literal meaning of इस्त्री is इ + स्त्री। इ as स्वर विभक्ति means objectification. स्त्री in turn means act of spreading. because स्त्री is itself स्तृञ् + इ = objectification of act of स्तृञ्. So स्त्री means objectification of spreading surface/cloth = act of spreading. and इस्त्री means objectification of act of spreading and hence iron.
For Indian langiages, इस्त्री is a new word coined only in last ~200 years.  It gained circulation because it got built on existing concept of स्तृ. And स्तृ was existing because its constituents, like we saw in case of ऋ and ऌ, had emerged from neural connection based meanings.

Keyur-Commentary/ऋऌक्.title: ऋऌक्
Keyur-Commentary/ऋऌक्.content:
ऋऌक्
Why Early Language Was Mutation-Proof
Long before dictionaries, teachers, or writing, language had only one possible way to work: the sound itself had to carry the meaning directly into the listener’s brain. This direct, intutive link between a sound (वर्ण) and its meaning is the neurosonic footprint. This is why we see a high degree of correlation between sound and meaning in a variety of languages[^1].
Imagine two dogs settling a fight.

Dog A growls low and long → superiority.
Dog B answers with a high, broken whine → surrender.

No dog ever explained this growl means I am boss. Every dog’s brain instantly recognises the meaning because the acoustic shape triggers the exact neural response evolution built for that situation. These two barks are वर्ण in dog language.
Now suppose one puppy’s superiority growl mutates and sounds like a playful yip. Other dogs do not understand. The mutated signal fails to trigger the correct circuits, leading to confusion, attack, or ignoring. The mutation dies with that puppy. The original sound-meaning pair survives unchanged because it is anchored in the shared wiring of the dog brain.
Early Hominini language worked the same way.
In the era of Homo erectus, and earlier, there was no possibility of teaching arbitrary word meanings. The only sounds that could become वर्ण - uniquely identifiable sound with built-in meaning - were those whose physical shape (frequency, rhythm, articulation, formants) directly activated the right neural circuits in every listener’s brain.
Because meaning was wired into the brain itself, mutation was almost impossible:

A वर्ण whose sound no longer matched the neural target simply failed to communicate.
Listeners did not learn the “wrong” meaning; they just did not understand — like the dogs with the mutated growl.
The incorrect variant died out in one generation.
Only वर्ण that fitted the shared brain circuitry survived and spread.

This is why proto-language needed no teaching of meanings: the वर्ण already carried their meaning inside every skull. Teaching became necessary millions of years later, when संज्ञा revolution invented many words that needed means beyond direct neurosonic grounding.
In short: the first language sounds were mutation-proof because they were biological, not cultural. The brain itself was the dictionary, and any misspelling was fatal to the word. This is the true origin of language stability across deep time.
The वर्ण and their meanings are like fossils - unchanged over millions of years. Also, this is why they are considered [स्वयंभु वा स्वयं प्रोक्ता - पाणिनीयशिक्षा-3] (ashtadhyayi.com/shiksha). Because वर्ण and their meanings are hard wired in brains, they are considered अ-पौरुषेय - not created by any human.
The superiority growl has survived as ऋ and the submission growl has survived as ऌ. Although these two वर्ण had evolved way before mammals, they were very much part of the vocabulary of Homo erectus and were included in शिव सूत्र when the same was compiled.
This fits perfectly with two key technical properties of ऋ and ऌ.


ऋ and ऌ. are स्वर and are distinctly different from वर्ण thet are produced by mouth parts touching each other -[स्पर्शानाम् पाणिनीयशिक्षा - ४ ] (ashtadhyayi.com/shiksha). We Homo Sapiens can’t pronounce ऋ and ऌ without tongue touching other parts of the mouth. But this was possible for Homo erectus (or some other species that compiled शॉव सूत्र.) We can understand original sounds if we hold the tongue with two fingers and try to pronounce ऋ and ऌ.


Because ऌ has a tendency to quiver when elongated and does not remain a continuous sound, it has ह्रस्व and प्लुत forms but does not have दीर्घ form. In a दीर्घ (2 मात्रा) duration, pronunciation stops at the pause, causing quivering, and ऌ becomes ह्रस्व.


Besides this ऋ and ऌ aspect, there are many other linguistic indicators suggesting that the concept of शिव has deep roots, indicating to Homo erectus (or at least bipedalism) as the species that compiled शिव सूत्र. This makes the time frame for शिव सूत्र compilation somewhere between 1 lakh year ago to 20/30 lakh years ago.

Keyur-Commentary/डुकृञ्-Revolution.title: डुकृञ् Revolution
Keyur-Commentary/डुकृञ्-Revolution.content:
डुकृञ् is a मूल धातु in Sanskrit and it means “to do.”
Deciphering डुकृञ् meaning from its constituent वर्ण meanings gives generates one  very interesting interpretation. In proto Sanskrit it means - Be ware (उ of ड) maneuver/stone (क) superior(ऋ)  surface (ञ). This is verbal instructions for making and using stone tools.
By ~33 lakh years ago (goin by evidence at Lomekwi),  Homonini had figured out how to make and use stone tools.
Up to this point, like rest of animals, Hominin  had  infinite LOOP akin to REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) of Unix as default in their brain’s operating system. In animals, we can say instead of print the default output was muscle movement, what we now refer to by word “act” - for animals it is like REAL (Read-Eval-Act-Loop) .   So the OS was at rest waiting to be  triggered by environment.
There were always some individuals whose resting loop was “Seek-Act-Evaluate-Loop” (SAEL) These were monkeys always seeking to “do” something, irrespective of whether required or not. Kids whose explore function never turned off. In normal world, i assume, such individuals ended up in mouth of lions more often and their population remained in check. Most of specie remained in idle loop if environment did not change, there was no action.
My hypothesis is that this stone tool event caused individuals with SAEL loop focused on action to be preferentially selected by evolution. Tool user had and have advantage over non user. As a result downstream Hominini and consequently nearly all Humans have this loop as default setting. One continuously seeks to do something, irrespective of whether it is required or not.
The infinite loop in brain OS for most humans is “urge to do”, something डुकृञ् reflects in language; instead of “urge to observe” for most animals.
Because this loop is motivation loop and is rooted in limbic - animal brain - it is beyond direct control of “thinking” cortical brain.
I believe this is when language started to differentiating verbs from hitherto undifferentiated words (धातु / वर्ण समास) used as both - verbs and nouns. In chronology of evolution of speech, डुकृञ् revolution occurred after संज्ञा revolution and before evolution of तिङ्.

Keyur-Commentary/तिङ्.content:
तिङ् प्रत्यय are sub section of लस्य.
तिङ् प्रत्यय are instruction set referring to action required to dock and launch boats. the action required depends on three parameters.

Whether purpose is to launch or dock boat this is direction of oar (पद).
anchorage - on beach, in basin or in deep sea. The word for anchor is - verb(rope) water up pointed = पुरुष
Draft of the ship. This is measured in single wave equivalent, two wave equivalent or more than two waves.




























































पदपरस्मैआत्मनेपुरुषएकद्विबहुएकद्विबहुप्रथमतिप्तस्झितआताम्झमध्यमसिप्थस्थथास्आथाम्ध्वम्उत्तममिप्वस्मस्इट्/डवहिमहिङ्
==पद==
पद mans paddle/oar. There are two directions in which one can paddle. towards shore and towards sea. Hence there are two types of पद - आत्मनै and परस्मै
==पुरुष==
There are three locations where a boat can be anchored. प्रथम  पुरुष means anchoring on/near beach. मध्यम पुरुष means anchorage which is like basins adjacent to pier. उत्तम पुरुष means deep sea anchor.
==वचन==
वचन refers to draft of the boat measured in height of wave/person. एक वचन means draft is such that you can receive boat with hands/legs द्वि वचन means draft is such that it needs rolling in wave - tide.  बहु वचन means draft is such that boat is constrained hard/tight outward.
Actions Grid
~15 lakh years ago, these were memorized by students the way multiplication tables were memorized. These were added as suffixes to all actions as meaning modifiers.

परस्मैपद = when you are launching boat

प्रथमपुरुषः =  when you are anchored at shore and want to launch boat

एकवचन = if you want to launch boar, are anchored at shore and your boat has draft equal to one limb (क); then do तिप् = त इ प = float below oar = oar when boat gets afloat
द्विवचन = if you want to launch boar, are anchored at shore and your boat has draft equal to depth of tide; then do तस् = त स float (in) basin or make furrow for float  or float align (wait and alilgn floating to tide)
बहुवचन = if you want to launch boar, are anchored at shore and your boat needs draft beyond depth of high tide; do झि = झ इ = vibrate (boat) inward


मध्यमपुरुषः = you are anchored at pier with basin

एकवचन = if you want to launch boat, are anchored at a basin with pier and your boat has draft equal to one limb = सिप् = स इ प = object(basin) oar =  oar in basin
द्विवचनम् = if you want to launch boat and boat is anchored at basin+pier and draft of boat is equal to high tide = थस् = थ स =(use) platform furrow
बहुवचनम् = if you want to launch boat and boat is anchored at basin+pier and draft of boat is more than high tide = थ = थ = (use) platform


उत्तमपुरुषः =  you are anchored at deep sea

एकवचन = you want to launch boat, anchored at deep sea and draft is equal to one wave; then मिप् = म इ प = oar inside
द्विवचनम् = you want to launch boat, anchored at deep sea and draft is equal to high tide = वस् = व स = persons gathered = launch when persons are gathered OR launch when waves are calm. because docking is done at deep sea only when waves were hard, launch only when waves are calm.
बहुवचनम् = you want to launch boat, anchored at deep sea and draft is more than depth of tide = मस् = म स = inside gathered = launch when inside is gathered OR lauch when inside is calm. Because docking is done at deep sea only when shore is rocky, launch  when inside waters are calm




आत्मनेपदम् = When docking

प्रथमपुरुषः = when you need to reach shore

एकवचनम् with small draft boat; त = float
द्विवचनम् draft equal to high tide = आताम् = अ त अ म = untill float untill inside
बहुवचनम् = when draft is mroe than high tide = झ = vibrate


मध्यमपुरुषः = set up is pier with basins

एकवचनम् = थास् = थ अ स = platform up to basin
द्विवचनम् =  आथाम् =  अ थ अ म = upto pier upto inside = when water depth is upto platform
बहुवचनम् = ध्वम् = ध व म = carry person inside =  unload before taking to basin and pier


उत्तमपुरुषः = when docking at deep sea

एकवचनम् draft is equal to limb = इड् = इ ड = below fear  = If there is fear from below, then only dock at deep sea with small boat

बहुवचन = when docking a deep draft boat at deep sea; महिङ् = म ह इ ङ = inside object(hard) periphery/outward = inside hard below periphery OR inside object(hard)  outside = rocky shore.

Keyur-Commentary/धातु-पाठ-as-linguistic-.title: धातु पाठ as linguistic fossil
Keyur-Commentary/धातु-पाठ-as-linguistic-.content:
When language emerged/evolved, it must have used sounds, the meaning of which were understood intuitively. Because there was nothing to learn from, meanings had to be intuitive - स्वयंभू and स्वयंप्रोक्त. I believe these sounds evolved to become वर्ण. these - वर्ण and its built-in meanings - would have evolved into more complex composite sounds and meanings। 
Morphologically पद are derived from धातु and प्रत्यय. The meaning of पद is also derived from the meaning of धातु and प्रत्यय. Sanskrit is special because it claims that all words are derived words. For most word derivation is known with the help of पाणिनि अष्टाध्यायी.
धातु and प्रत्यय are made from वर्ण. If we extend the logic that everything is derived, the meanings of धातु and प्रत्यय must be derived from their constituent वर्ण. In the absence of guidance similar to अष्टाध्यायी and धातु पाठ, we have to decipher rules and वर्ण meanings to understand this process.
Primitive intuitive meanings of वर्ण are no longer self-evident to us today because we have overused language, and intuitive meanings are lost in the clutter. However, because धातु and their meanings are preserved, we can attempt to decipher the intuitive meanings of वर्ण. After that, we can try to arrive at rules for deriving धातुs and their meanings from the meaning of constituent वर्ण. 
I am working on this hypothesis and would like to present some interesting possibilities.
